tests.question: Do preregistered non-Kerr compact-object models predict the measured morphology and interferometric observables better than Kerr model families after complexity penalties?
tests.observable: Held-out predictive fit and morphology consistency for Kerr and specified non-Kerr forward-model ensembles.
tests.method: Generate comparable radiative-transfer ensembles under registered Kerr and non-Kerr metrics; fit training observables and evaluate held-out visibility, closure, morphology, and polarization targets.
tests.support_condition: A specified non-Kerr family provides materially better held-out predictions or uniquely explains observables that Kerr families fail under comparable assumptions.
tests.refutation_condition: The specified non-Kerr family fails preregistered observables or is excluded within declared parameter bounds while Kerr families remain viable.
tests.inconclusive_condition: Plasma uncertainties dominate metric differences, priors are not comparable, or the test excludes only a narrow non-Kerr family.

tests.question: Do non-Kerr and Kerr families make distinguishable preregistered predictions for future multi-epoch morphology or polarization?
tests.observable: Future epoch measurements that separate registered model-family prediction intervals.
tests.method: Freeze prediction distributions before acquiring or unblinding later-epoch data; evaluate coverage and model discrimination with a registered scoring rule.
tests.support_condition: Later observations fall inside a non-Kerr prediction region and outside the Kerr prediction region under the registered scoring rule.
tests.refutation_condition: Later observations exclude the specified non-Kerr prediction region while remaining consistent with Kerr predictions.
tests.inconclusive_condition: Prediction intervals overlap strongly or later observations lack sufficient sensitivity.

independence_requirements: Metric families and parameter priors must be fixed before evaluation.
Plasma and radiative-transfer assumptions must be matched as fairly as possible across model families.
At least one observable must be held out or genuinely future.
Refutation applies only to explicitly registered non-Kerr families and parameter ranges.
limitations: No finite test can refute the unrestricted class of all non-Kerr compact objects.
Image morphology alone is strongly entangled with plasma and radiative-transfer assumptions.
